dedupe_keys.name: gdemm2024 global digital elevation merged model

description: GFZ Data Services publishes GDEMM2024, a global 30-arcsecond merged elevation and relief grid suite under CC BY 4.0. The own DOI record identifies surface, bedrock, ice-thickness, land-type and geoid layers, with one-arcminute downsampled versions. The article says grids refer to a common vertical datum and reports checks against about 22,000 GNSS stations for the surface layer. These rasters can supply terrain, bathymetry or ice geometry to regional flood, transport exposure or infrastructure siting simulations. A caveat is that a global merged product combines source DEMs with different acquisition dates and errors; local engineering analysis may need higher-resolution surveys. Users must preserve datum and mask semantics when extracting an area. I read the own GFZ page, DOI metadata and article Data Records without downloading rasters, measuring local accuracy or running an inundation model. No directly related catalogue record was identified. GeoTIFF files are available through the GFZ Data Services DOI.
